argument:
The bear's financing bridge is valid: RM141m after specified finance and lease deductions cannot cover RM486m owner dividends. The counterargument concerns the operating engine rather than defending that payout. Excluding MFRS129, revenue grew 7% and EBITDA 14%; H1 ex-EI profit rose 22%. These separate observations support operating improvement beyond inflation accounting and exceptional items.

Cash after the conservative deductions remained positive, albeit narrow, so investment and financing costs did not consume all observed cash. A purchase scenario is stronger recurring earnings and retained cash reducing dependence on debt; any payout adjustment would be prospective, not a reported decision. Net debt and Singapore admissions weakness require restraint at 30.38x trailing earnings. The optimistic case is profitable hospital growth converting into financial repair, not a high-dividend or already-deleveraged story.
key_points: Underlying operating improvement survives accounting/item normalization.
Conservative post-financing cash is positive but insufficient for dividends.
Financial repair requires retained cash and continued delivery.
rebuttal_to_previous: I concede payout undercoverage and leverage. Ex-MFRS129 EBITDA growth of 14% and ex-EI H1 profit growth of 22% substantiate an improving engine, while RM141m remains after financing/leases. That preserves a conditional retention-and-growth case without claiming the dividend is funded.
